Subject: Order form update — request to consolidate SOW line items + phased go-live

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. GridLogic has one small ask before we finalize the order form: we would like to consolidate two separate SOW line items ("Real-time Embeddings" and "Batch Embeddings") into a single combined embeddings SKU, and split the implementation into Phase 1 (pilot) and Phase 2 (scale). The commercial team needs: 

- A single line item to simplify internal chargeback (with clear usage buckets for pilot vs scale)
- A revised implementation schedule with milestone-based acceptance (pilot: 6 weeks, scale: +8 weeks)
- Prorated billing guidance for the pilot month and mid-quarter start

I've attached our preferred wording in GridLogic_OrderForm_v3.pdf and a marked-up Exhibit A for SOW changes. Can you route this to legal/pricing and confirm whether Redwood can accept the consolidation and phased acceptance language? We also want to make sure SLA ramp dates and credit triggers are preserved.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to sign by end of next week.

Best,
Alicia Torres
Head of Commercial Operations
GridLogic

Marcus / team — reviewed GridLogic_OrderForm_v3.pdf and SOW redlines. High-level legal guidance below: 

1) Consolidated SKU language 
- Acceptable in principle. Recommend adding a short parenthetical clarifying the pilot usage buckets vs scale buckets and referencing the MSA "Usage Definitions" addendum to avoid ambiguity.

2) Acceptance and credit triggers 
- Move the acceptance criteria into Exhibit F (acceptance milestones) rather than burying them in the Order Form. This keeps alignment with Section 6.1 (Acceptance) of the MSA.
- For the SLA credit triggers during pilot, carve out a limited credit cap (e.g., 10% of pilot month fees) — commercial may want more, but that's a negotiation point.

3) Proration / mid-quarter starts 
- We can do pro rata invoicing for pilot month. Need to confirm invoicing cut dates with finance (Stephanie, loop in billing if we hit mid-month start).

4) Redline suggestions (attached) 
- I made inline edits to Exhibit A (SOW_ExhibitA_redlines.docx). Also propose a short defined term: "Pilot Period" (start date, end date, acceptance milestone).

Please let me know if you want legal to push a tracked-changes PDF back to GridLogic or if sales ops should consolidate pricing first. I can turn this around same-day.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_ExhibitA_redlines.docx (DOCX, tracked changes)

Quick pricing/ops note: 

- Consolidation is straightforward if GridLogic accepts a single committed throughput commitment mapped to usage bands. We should avoid introducing a new tier for this one deal.
- Recommended pricing approach: keep the same per-unit fee as Batch Embeddings for combined SKU, and create a temporary discounted pilot bucket (15% off list) for first 3 months tied to the Pilot Period. After scale acceptance, revert to standard committed pricing; any overages bill at published overage rate.
- Implementation resource note: pilot will require one dedicated solutions engineer for the 6-week window plus a 2-week overlap into scale for runbook handoff. That labor should be captured as an implementation line item or as a time-and-materials estimate — call out in Exhibit A.
- Billing/proration: finance can support pro rata invoicing but needs explicit dates. Stephanie, can you confirm earliest realistic start date and invoice alignment?

If legal is happy, I'll update the price sheet and send a clean PDF back to Alicia.

Karthik
Director, Pricing & Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

- Legal (Laura) is comfortable with the consolidated SKU; she suggests we move explicit acceptance language into Exhibit F and introduce the defined term "Pilot Period". Laura attached a tracked-changes doc — copy attached here.
- Pricing (Karthik) recommends we keep the combined SKU at the Batch Embeddings per-unit rate, with a temporary pilot discount (15% off) for the first 3 months and a capped pilot-credit (10% of pilot month fees) for SLA misses.
